models.note: Local coder models for PACER coding. Court text never leaves the machine: models run through a local Ollama server and are pinned by content digest; the coder refuses a model whose digest differs. Pull with `ollama pull <name>`; weights live in Ollama's store (~/.ollama), not in the repository.

runtime.start: env $(the env above) ollama serve   # a dedicated server for this pipeline; one model in memory at a time
runtime.note: two requests in flight on a 16 GB machine: four were barely faster on real filings and added about 2.5 GB of KV cache

coder_A.why: best accuracy of the candidates on dev cases (event F1 0.87, action 0.91) at 7.9 s per page

coder_B.why: a second model family (Llama), so the coders do not share errors; 7.1 s per page

selection.how: python -m state_machines.coding.select_models on dev cases synth_001-005 (held-out never used)

rejected.qwen3:8b: 29.6 s/page, event F1 0.80: slower and not better
rejected.llama3.1:8b: about 50 s/page under prompt 1.1: too slow on 16 GB

reliability_real_cases.note: agreement on acts the models coded; the docket parser's acts are excluded

documented.title: Level 1. Which listed platforms do the records name, in how many cases?

withheld.title: Level 1. Which services does a record refer to by a placeholder, case by case? (A label means nothing outside its case.)

described.title: Level 1. Which generic descriptions of an online service do the records use? (Not platforms; no use claimed.)

features.title: Level 1. Which feature phrases do the records state, under which CAC class?

reconstructed.title: Level 2. Which acts did both coders agree on?

disputed.title: Between levels 1 and 3. Where does a sentence state a platform or feature as a means while the two coders dispute the act? (No act is published there.)

supported.title: Level 3. Where does a record state that an act was done by means of a platform or feature?
supported.sparql:
PREFIX oa: <http://www.w3.org/ns/oa#>
PREFIX core: <https://ontology.unifiedcyberontology.org/uco/core/>
PREFIX action: <https://ontology.unifiedcyberontology.org/uco/action/>
PREFIX clt: <https://w3id.org/caselinker/trajectory#>
SELECT DISTINCT ?case ?event ?action ?relationship ?what ?phrase ?standing WHERE {
  GRAPH ?og { ?obs oa:motivatedBy ?m ; oa:hasTarget ?span ; oa:hasBody ?body ; clt:sourceStatus ?standing .
              ?evidence oa:hasTarget ?span ; oa:hasBody ?rel . FILTER(?evidence != ?obs)
              OPTIONAL { ?obs clt:featureTerm ?phrase } OPTIONAL { ?body core:name ?name } }
  GRAPH ?rg { ?rel core:kindOfRelationship ?relationship ; core:source ?s ; core:target ?t }
  GRAPH ?eg { ?act clt:actionCode ?action } FILTER(?act IN (?s, ?t)) FILTER(STRENDS(STR(?eg), ":evidence"))
  FILTER(?m != oa:describing)
  FILTER(?body IN (?s, ?t) || (BOUND(?phrase) && EXISTS { GRAPH ?any { ?s a ?body } }))
  BIND(COALESCE(?name, REPLACE(STR(?body), "^.*#", "")) AS ?what)
  BIND(REPLACE(REPLACE(STR(?og), "^urn:caselinker:pacer:", ""), ":observations$", "") AS ?case)
  BIND(REPLACE(STR(?act), "^.*[/#:-](e[0-9]+)$", "$1") AS ?event)
} ORDER BY ?case ?event ?what

resolve-1.0.0.heldout._note: Rules resolve-1.0.0. Held-out cases were scored beside dev in four code states while the coder was developed on 2026-11-17 (resolved recall 98, 138, 141, then 148 of 228); this is the last of those. A second development register, not a blind set.

resolve-1.1.0.confirm._note: The one scoring of this split under resolve-1.1.0, after the rules were frozen and committed. Wording written without sight of the rules. The pages were first coded earlier the same day under pre-freeze code and were not scored then; this run is a second coding under the committed rules.

resolve-1.1.0.dev._note: Rules were developed on these cases.

resolve-1.1.0.heldout._note: A later look: these cases had been scored repeatedly during coder development under resolve-1.0.0 before the 1.1.0 rules were written. No 1.1.0 rule was written against them, but they are not a blind set.

resolve-1.2.0.confirm._note: resolve-1.2.0: level C needs the sentence to state the feature as the means (the stated-means rule shared with the observation layer); an offender act coded on a rule or policy statement is dropped. Re-scored from the cached model answers with the earlier results already seen, so no split is a first look, and the rule was not tuned on held-out or confirm. In the resolved coding only the level-C rows differ from 1.1.0 on every split; each coder's own rows can differ where an act on a rule statement is dropped (coder B precision on confirm 181/304 becomes 181/296).
